clue.text: I'm probing sore with end of pointed instrument

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so take the last letter of pointed
something probing a wound goes into it, so these letters sit inside the other piece

parts.note: an ulcer is a sore
I'm written without the apostrophe gives IM

explanation.surface: Someone poking at a wound with the tip of a sharp tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instrument' looks like the sharp tool in the surface, but it is a musical one.
explanation.definitionFit: A dulcimer is a stringed musical instrument struck with small hammers.

clue.text: Fellow out of work shows fulsomeness

indicators.note: something out of a piece has left it, so the letter for fellow is removed

parts.note: a function is a job or work something does

explanation.surface: A man who has lost his job is laying on the flattery.
explanation.definitionFit: Unction can mean an excessive, oily earnestness of manner, which is what fulsomeness describes.

clue.text: Johnny retains small university apartments in America

indicators.note: a container that retains something holds it inside, so the other pieces go within

parts.note: johnny is British slang for a condom
mini means small

explanation.surface: A man named Johnny keeps a little college flat in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: MINIU goes inside CONDOM, between its second O and the M. 'Johnny' (rubber johnny) is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a condominium is a block of individually owned flats, so apartments in the US.

clue.text: Slough hospital is after damages

indicators.note: one piece being after another means it follows it, so the hospital letter comes last

parts.note: to mar is to damage, so mars means damages
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Reads as news that the hospital in the town of Slough has been damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is a town west of London, but here it is the common noun: a swampy hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: A slough is a boggy, waterlogged patch of ground, a synonym for a wetland.

clue.text: Devastating effects of storms gripping Virginia

indicators.note: something gripping another holds it tightly inside

parts.note: rages means storms, as a gale storms or rages
VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: The damage left by storms that hit the state of Virginia.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravages are the destructive results of something, such as the toll of war or time.

clue.text: To son, clothing still matters

indicators.note: clothing something wraps around it, so the pair of pieces goes around the other

parts.note: a still is a photograph, a pic

explanation.surface: Someone telling their son that his clothes still matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' is a noun here, a photograph, not an adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Topics are subjects under discussion, the matters at hand.

clue.text: Jockey got extremely bored in Kentish Town

indicators.note: to jockey is to jostle and manoeuvre, so these letters are pushed into a new order
a word taken extremely is just its two outside letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A jockey who got very bored while staying in a Kent town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' applies to got, giving GT; GT, BORED and IN are rearranged. Kentish Town is also a district of London, but here Tonbridge is a town in Kent, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonbridge is a market town in the English county of Kent, so a Kentish town.

clue.text: Highly acidic letter from Rhodes?

definitions.meaning: a strongly acidic liquid has a pH of 1, written here with the roman one
Rhodes is a Greek island, so this is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Suggests a very sharp-tongued letter written from the island of Rhodes.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is PH plus I (the roman numeral one): pH 1 is extremely acidic. The question mark flags Rhodes as standing for Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Phi is the twenty-first character of the Greek alphabet, used on Rhodes as across Greece.

clue.text: Enclose report of inmate's good health?

parts.note: the clue reads as a report saying the inmate's (the con is) well; a con, or convict, is a prison inmate
being fine means being in good health

explanation.surface: A prison bulletin announcing that a prisoner is well.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as a report saying 'con's fine': the prisoner is well. Those two words joined give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To confine is to keep within limits or shut in, so to enclose.

clue.text: Breach of agreement involving cunning backtracking

indicators.note: involving means including within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a convention is a formal agreement, such as a treaty

indicators.note: backtracking goes back the way it came, so the word for cunning is read backwards

parts.note: art can mean cunning or craft, as in artful

explanation.surface: A broken treaty where someone sneakily went back on their word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backtracking' makes TRA from ART, and 'involving' sets it inside CONVENTION after CON.
explanation.definitionFit: A contravention is a violation of a rule or law, so a breach of it.

clue.text: Block in path, so bikers turned back

indicators.note: turned back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Cyclists on a path being blocked and made to turn round.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters HSOBIK sit inside 'path, so bikers'; 'turned back' reverses them. 'in' marks the concealment.
explanation.definitionFit: To put the kibosh on something is to stop it, so as a verb it means to block or scupper.

clue.text: Keeping quiet, winger fouled scorer

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it, so the quiet letters go inside
fouled means messed up, so the letters of winger are jumbled

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A football match: a winger is fouled but keeps quiet, and still scores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scorer' is not a goalscorer but someone who writes musical scores.
explanation.definitionFit: George Gershwin was an American composer, and a composer scores music.

clue.text: Cast hit with crisis on producing melodrama

indicators.note: to cast is to throw about, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cast scoring a hit with a show about a crisis, staging a melodrama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like the actors in a play, but it is the instruction to rearrange HIT, CRISIS and ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Histrionics is exaggerated, theatrical behaviour, the same overblown emotion as a melodrama.

clue.text: Ailing suspect is spied on by old copper

indicators.note: suspect can mean dubious or unsound, so these letters are not in their proper order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
D stood for the old British penny, a copper coin before decimal currency

explanation.surface: A sick suspect is watched by a retired policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges IS SPIED and ON; 'by' adds D. 'copper' looks like a police officer, but it is a coin: the old penny, written d.
explanation.definitionFit: Indisposed is a polite word for slightly unwell, so ailing.

clue.text: Youthful local employee's first on track

parts.note: in Britain a local is a nearby pub

indicators.note: first takes only the opening letter of employee

parts.note: a scent is a trail, the track a hound follows

explanation.surface: A young pub worker's first day following a trail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' is British for one's neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Pubescent describes someone at or reaching puberty, so young or youthful.

clue.text: The woman had to get rid of small building

definitions.meaning: she had, contracted with an apostrophe
to cast off or discard, as a tree drops its leaves
a hut or outbuilding for storing tools

explanation.surface: A woman had to clear out a small outbuilding.
explanation.walkthrough: Three readings in a row: the contraction she'd, the verb meaning to discard, and the garden hut.
explanation.definitionFit: Each sense fits: a contraction of she had, a verb for casting off, and a noun for a hut.

clue.text: Wine in a jug? Not right

indicators.note: not right tells us to leave out the letter for right

parts.note: jug and stir are both slang for prison

explanation.surface: Someone complaining that wine served in a jug is not correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jug' is not a pitcher but prison slang, as is STIR; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine from the Piedmont region.

clue.text: Dog jumps about, entertaining half of nick

indicators.note: a host entertaining a guest has them inside, so the half word goes within
about means turned round, so the word for jumps is read backwards

parts.note: leaps means jumps

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is its first two letters

explanation.surface: A dog leaping around, holding on to part of something it stole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes SPAEL; 'nick' is British slang for steal, but here only its letters matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaniel is a breed of dog with long drooping ears.

clue.text: Sweeper about to control start of game will be man of the match

indicators.note: about means around, so the broom wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: a broom is a sweeper
to ride a horse is to control it

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A football sweeper set to dominate from kick-off will be the star player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man of the match' suggests a football award; here the match is a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage is a match, and the groom is the male half of it.

clue.text: At home on night off? It's the latest fad

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters of night are scrambled

explanation.surface: Staying in on a night off has become the fashionable thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-thing is something fashionable at the moment, a current craze.

clue.text: Offensive smell rises over locale

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from bottom to top, so the word for smell is backwards

parts.note: BO is body odour, a bad smell
a scene is a place where something happens, a locale

explanation.surface: A nasty smell drifting up over a neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' turns the smell upward, and 'over' places it above the locale in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene means offensive to accepted standards of decency.

clue.text: Rodent bites small European monkey

indicators.note: biting something holds it between the teeth, so the pieces go inside

parts.note: a marmot is a burrowing rodent

explanation.surface: A rodent biting a small European monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'monkey' looks like part of the victim's description, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A marmoset is a small South American primate, a type of monkey.

clue.text: Smooth guy, gutted, accepts defeat

indicators.note: accepting something takes it in, so the defeat goes inside
a word gutted loses its insides, leaving its outer letters

parts.note: a loss is a defeat

explanation.surface: A slick man, heartbroken, acknowledges he has lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' looks like British slang for devastated, but it empties the word guy of its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Glossy means having a shiny, sleek surface, so smooth.

clue.text: Pick up from bottom of skiing slope

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter

parts.note: to lean is to slope or tilt

explanation.surface: Collecting something at the foot of the ski run.
explanation.definitionFit: To glean is to gather or collect bit by bit, as information is picked up.

clue.text: Already started working as a plumber?

definitions.text: Already started working as a plumber?

parts.words: Already started working as a plumber?
parts.note: a plumber at work is literally inside the pipe-work; the phrase also means already under way

explanation.surface: Asks whether someone has begun a job in plumbing.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for something in progress is pictured literally as a plumber at work inside the pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the pipeline means being under way or in preparation, so already started.

clue.text: Can Congress upset Nationalist?

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word for congress is read backwards

parts.note: it is a coy word for sex, and congress means sexual intercourse

explanation.surface: Asks whether the US Congress can overturn a nationalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Congress' is not the US legislature but sexual congress, IT; 'upset' makes TI.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin is a metal can for food, as in a tin of beans.

clue.text: Conspiracist's conclusion on flat Earth?

parts.note: plane means flat, as a plane surface

indicators.note: a word's conclusion is its final letter

explanation.surface: A flat-earther's conclusion about the shape of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conclusion on flat' puts T after PLANE in this across entry. The question mark marks Earth as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is one example of a world orbiting the Sun, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Joker ensnares Batman finally? That's criminal!

indicators.note: ensnaring traps something inside, so the letter goes within

parts.note: a gagster is a joker, someone who tells gags

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of Batman

explanation.surface: Batman's foe the Joker traps the hero at last: a villainous act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joker' wants to be the Batman villain; it is a gagster, which traps N.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangster is a member of a gang of violent criminals.
